summary: Staggered control-plane commit window suppresses primary model selection, sporadic fallback to secondary variant
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled weighted rollout for rwinference-gpt-3.8b-v1 (BrightCart dedicated pool), several customer sessions observed degraded outputs and elevated latencies. Investigation showed requests that should have been routed to the primary variant were intermittently routed to the older secondary variant for short windows of time.

Impact: BrightCart reported a 7-9% increase in error and quality complaints in the checkout assistant flows for a 45-minute span. Latency for affected requests increased from median 120ms to median 410ms and a 99th percentile spike to ~1.8s. No data leakage observed; this is routing/selection behavior only.

Environment: Dedicated pool (BrightCart-reserved), prod, us-west-2. Canary rollout weight was 20%, staged over a 30-minute window. Control-plane commit for the rollout occurred at 2026-01-27T14:03:22Z. Edge caches were observed to have staggered TTL expirations.

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Initiate request with tenant header X-Tenant: brightcart and session cookie present.
2) Orchestrator commit applies rollout at control-plane time T0 (2026-01-27T14:03:22Z).
3) A subset of edge nodes retained previous route mapping until their routing cache TTLs expired between T0+90s and T0+600s, causing session affinity lookup against legacy shards.
4) Requests that hit those edges were routed to the secondary variant until cache refresh.

Relevant logs/snippets: 
- Orchestrator commit: commit_id=cf3a9b2, time=2026-01-27T14:03:22Z
- Edge cache debug: edge-node-usw2-12 cache-epoch=1024 ttl_remaining_ms=120000 (first affected)
- Sample request id that observed fallback: req=rc-6428c41b, ts=2026-01-27T14:05:09Z, routed_variant=rwinference-gpt-3.8b-v1-compat-secondary, latency_ms=532
- Tracing link: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/rc-6428c41b
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger a staged rollout commit in dedicated pool
Issue requests from a session with X-Tenant header to edge nodes
Observe edge cache TTL and routing table update delays
Compare variant selected by orchestrator vs edge logs

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: rollback or model eviction caused selection to fallback — disproved by commit logs showing no rollback until after customer alert
Edge TTLs were heterogeneous due to a previous staggered deployment of edge-proxy that set inconsistent default TTLs (reported in edge-proxy PR #134)

Control plane successfully updated routing policy; however, the edge fleet applied updates on a per-node asynchronous path, and some nodes prioritized local cache expiration over immediate invalidation signals
Observed correlation between nodes that refused or delayed SSE/invalidations (403/504) and requests that routed to secondary variant
No GPU preemption or autoscaler events during incident window — serving-runtime health checks remained green

root_cause: A recent edge-proxy configuration change (PR #134) left routing cache TTL behaviour unset on a subset of nodes. When the control-plane committed the staged rollout, some edge nodes did not receive or apply immediate invalidation signals and instead relied on long heterogeneous TTLs. This caused a temporary mismatch between control-plane routing policy and edge routing tables, resulting in intermittent routing to the older secondary variant until each node's cache expired or the invalidation channel succeeded.
resolution: 1) Emergency mitigation: broadcast explicit invalidation signal to whole edge fleet and temporarily widened orchestrator canary window to 0% on affected tenant to stop further customer impact. 2) Rolled hotfix for edge-proxy default TTL and strengthened invalidation acknowledgement (edge-proxy v1.7.3). 3) Orchestrator was patched to emit a forced cache-bust event on commit for dedicated pools where explicit invalidation feature flag is not negotiated. 4) Post-incident monitoring added to detect TTL skew across edge fleet and to alert when >2% of nodes have TTL variance >300s relative to control-plane expectation.
follow_up_tasks: Backfill automated test to verify invalidation ack path during PR rollouts (ENG-3987)
Add dashboard for edge cache TTL variance and rollout application lag (OBS-2201)
Run retro with edge/infra teams to tighten release checklist for TTL defaults and feature flags (scheduled 2026-02-05)
Communicate incident summary and customer impact to BrightCart CS contact and credit 10% of Jan usage for affected routes
